slot.brief: Three non-parallel forces in equilibrium; resolve components to find unknown force magnitude/angle.

stem: A point object is in equilibrium under three coplanar concurrent forces. Two of the forces are 4 N along the positive x-axis and 4 N at 60 degrees with the positive x-axis. The magnitude of the third force is

verdicts.working: The two forces sum to (6, 2√3) N, so their resultant has magnitude √(36 + 12) = 4√3 N. The third force must have the same magnitude to balance it.

working:
Resolve the second force: F2 = (4 cos 60 deg, 4 sin 60 deg) = (2, 2 sqrt 3).
First force F1 = (4, 0).
Resultant of the two known forces = (4 + 2, 0 + 2 sqrt 3) = (6, 2 sqrt 3).
Magnitude = sqrt(6^2 + (2 sqrt 3)^2) = sqrt(36 + 12) = sqrt 48 = 4 sqrt 3 N.
For equilibrium, the third force must balance this resultant, so its magnitude is also 4 sqrt 3 N.

Independent check: The two forces sum to (6, 2√3) N, so their resultant has magnitude √(36 + 12) = 4√3 N. The third force must have the same magnitude to balance it.
solution:
The resultant of the two known forces is $\vec R=(4+4\cos60^\circ,\,4\sin60^\circ)=(6,2\sqrt3)\,\text{N}$. 
$$|\vec R|=\sqrt{6^2+(2\sqrt3)^2}=4\sqrt3\,\text{N}$$
For equilibrium, the third force must be equal and opposite to this resultant; its magnitude is $4\sqrt3\,\text{N}$.
